title: The Promises the Afghanistan War Left Behind
gist: A retrospective on the August 2021 Kabul evacuation through Marine veteran Joe Laude, now executive director of the Operation Allies Refuge Foundation, highlighting the moral weight of gate decisions and the Afghans left behind after roughly 123,000 people were evacuated.

insights.claim: Approximately 123,000 people were evacuated from Kabul in August 2021 while thousands of Afghans sought a way out, and the last U.S. aircraft left on August 30, 2021.
insights.speaker: Zahra Rahimi
insights.so_what: Scale of the evacuation frames ongoing U.S. obligations to Afghan allies and resettlement policy debates.
insights.quote: approximately 123,000 people were evacuated and thousands of Afghans sought a way out
insights.locator: A Marine machine-gunner with Echo Company

insights.claim: Joe Laude, a Marine who served at Abbey Gate and now leads the Operation Allies Refuge Foundation, describes gate-access decisions during the evacuation as feeling like 'playing God' with Afghans' lives.
insights.speaker: Zahra Rahimi
insights.so_what: Veteran-led advocacy keeps pressure on U.S. policy toward Afghan allies, affecting credibility of U.S. commitments to partners.
insights.quote: “It felt almost like you were playing God with their life at that moment,”

insights.claim: The article argues the unresolved question of who was left behind continues to weigh on U.S. personnel, framing the war's end as leaving unfulfilled promises to Afghan partners.
insights.speaker: Zahra Rahimi
insights.so_what: Perceived abandonment of partners can erode U.S. alliance credibility elsewhere.
insights.quote: Who could he have helped? Who was left behind?
insights.locator: When the last U.S. aircraft departed
